subject: Cross-border exception request: short-term telemetry hop & DPA timing
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acutehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: dpo@acutehealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Short-term telemetry hop request + DPA amendment

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the call this morning. AcuteHealth has a short timeline to onboard your SDK into our analytics pipeline; we expect a two-week pilot. During initial rollout our analytics vendor requires a temporary routing step: aggregated telemetry for usage/latency metrics will be routed from our EU tenancy to Redwood's US analytics cluster for enrichment (no raw prompts to be stored in the US).

We need:
- Maximum temporary window: 72 hours per incident; overall pilot length: 14 days.
- Written confirmation that any data routed to the US will be encrypted in transit and at rest, that keys remain under Redwood control, and that persistent storage (full prompts or user PII) will not be retained in US clusters.
- Audit logging for every cross-border hop with an accessible sample log.
- A short DPA addendum reflecting the temporary processing exception and retention constraints.

I'm attaching a short operational runbook our ops team suggested (sample_operational_runbook.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet the above and share an ETA for the DPA amendment? Our legal team needs to sign before we can flip the switch.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Nguyen
Data Protection Officer
AcuteHealth

Attachment: sample_operational_runbook.pdf
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acutehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 10:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Short-term telemetry hop request + DPA amendment

Sara — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned that this should be narrow and strictly temporary. A few clarifying Qs before we circulate a DPA draft: 

1) Scope: when you say "aggregated telemetry", can you confirm whether traces will ever include hashed identifiers that could be re-linked to user records? If so we need to treat that as pseudonymous and restrict the hop further.
2) Retention during the hop: is 48 hours acceptable (Redwood can commit to 48 hours for analytics artifacts) or do you require the full 72-hour per-incident cap?
3) KMS expectations: do you need the Customer Managed Keys (CMK) to remain in EU control for the entire pipeline, or is a short-lived wrapping key acceptable for the US step?

I've attached a brief runbook we've been using for similar customers (residency_runbook.xlsx) that shows the operational controls and audit hooks. I'll loop in our legal and product folks once you confirm scope (cc'd).

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: residency_runbook.xlsx
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acutehealth.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 13:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Short-term telemetry hop request + DPA amendment

Team — quick legal read: we can support a narrowly scoped DPA addendum limited to the pilot and the specific telemetry types. Proposed guardrails: 
- Processing purpose: analytics/operational telemetry only (no content generation inputs, no raw prompts).
- Retention: audit/derived telemetry removed within 48 hours; allow up to 72 hours for edge cases with documented incident reason and prior notice.
- KMS: Customer keys remain in EU for primary storage; for the US analytics step we will use a wrapping key and provide key-use logs. We should avoid transferring unwrapped CMKs.
- Auditability: provide a sample of the cross-border hop logs (anonymized) and a dashboard link where the customer can query entries.

I'll draft a DPA amendment (first pass attached: DPA_amendment_v1.docx). Marissa/Stephanie — can you confirm if the product controls (hashing, no-persistence for prompts, audit streaming) are already implemented or need minor changes?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_amendment_v1.docx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acutehealth.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Short-term telemetry hop request + DPA amendment

Sara — thanks, quick technical confirmation from product/ops: 
- We will only route aggregated telemetry (metric counters, sampled latency histograms, anonymized error codes). No raw prompts or embeddings will be sent. Identifiers will be hashed with a one-way salt that is rotated daily.
- Retention: default retention in the US analytics cluster will be 48 hours. We can extend to 72 hours by exception with documented incident justification (consistent with Laura's note).
- KMS: primary data-at-rest uses your CMK in the EU. For the US hop we will use a short-lived envelope key (wrapping) created by Redwood; we will not persist customer CMKs outside EU. We will publish key-use audit logs to the dedicated audit stream.
- Audit logs: we can provide an anonymized sample and grant read-only access to the hop audit via a secure S3 link.

I've attached the KMS mapping export (KMS_mapping.csv) and will coordinate with Ops to prepare the log sample. Once Laura signs off on the DPA draft, Jonas — please send the DocuSign link to Sara and AcuteHealth legal to get execution started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference

Attachment: KMS_mapping.csv
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acutehealth.com>

Jonas/Laura/Marissa — that addresses our concerns. Two final asks before signature: 
1) Please provide the anonymized sample of the hop audit log (redacted PII) so our security team can validate the event fields.
2) Can Redwood commit to 24-hour notification SLA if any hop exceeds the planned retention window?

If both are confirmed we can proceed with the DPA amendment and sign on DocuSign. Please send the link when ready.

Thanks again,
